fields.Name: Microsoft Dynamics 365 (Dataverse)
fields.Description: Microsoft Dynamics 365 / Dataverse Web API (OData v4) connector for CE/model-driven app tables. OAuth2 client credentials (Entra ID); per-environment base URL; runtime EntityDefinitions discovery; change-tracking incremental; full CRUD.

Configuration.ScopeReason: These are distinct surfaces — different base URL, OAuth resource/audience, discovery, and (async) write semantics. MJ's membership/association clients consume the Dataverse-backed CE/model-driven apps; a single connector cannot honestly span Dataverse + F&O. Recorded for awareness; a future build can add an F&O connector without re-discovering.
Configuration.DiscoveryIsAuthoritativeRationale: The Dataverse EntityDefinitions endpoint (GET /api/data/v9.2/EntityDefinitions) enumerates the COMPLETE gamut of tables the credential can access — standard, custom, and solution-installed. Additionally GET /api/data/v9.2/ returns all EntitySet resources. Not a filtered subset. A comprehensive refresh may safely reversibly deactivate objects no longer in the response. Source: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-apps/developer/data-platform/webapi/overview and https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-apps/developer/data-platform/webapi/retrieve-metadata-name-metadataid.

universalPK.note: Every standard Dataverse table has a GUID PK named <entityLogicalName>id. URL path example: GET /api/data/v9.2/accounts(00000000-0000-0000-0000-000000000001); response body: 'accountid':'00000000-...'. Custom tables follow same pattern: <publisher_prefix>_<name>id. Source: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-apps/developer/data-platform/webapi/retrieve-entity-using-web-api.

Configuration.AuthFlowNote: Dataverse requires OAuth 2.0 for all non-.NET clients. Client Credentials grant (client_credentials) against Microsoft Entra ID is the server-to-server pattern. Scope: https://<orgname>.crm.dynamics.com/.default. Source: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-apps/developer/data-platform/authentication 'OAuth is the preferred means to authenticate' + 'If you are using anything other than .NET Framework, you must authenticate using OAuth.'
Configuration.TokenRefreshStrategyNote: Entra ID access tokens expire (typically 1 hour). Client credentials flow does not issue refresh_tokens — reacquire by re-running client_credentials grant. Cache and reacquire within ~5 min of expiry or on 401. Source: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-apps/developer/data-platform/authenticate-oauth.
Configuration.BaseURLTemplateNote: Per-environment URL. Region: crm=US, crm2=South America, crm7=Japan. Source: compose-http-requests docs table of URL parts at https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-apps/developer/data-platform/webapi/compose-http-requests-handle-errors.
Configuration.APIVersioningStrategyNote: Version in URL path: /api/data/v9.2/. v9.0/v9.1/v9.2 identical behaviors. v9.2 is current. Source: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-apps/developer/data-platform/webapi/web-api-versions.

PaginationDefaults.description: OData @odata.nextLink cursor pagination. Follow nextLink VERBATIM. Max page size 5,000. Prefer: odata.maxpagesize=N (max 5000). $skip NOT supported — do not use $top+$skip.
PaginationDefaults.source: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-apps/developer/data-platform/webapi/query/page-results: 'up to 5,000 table rows... The service ignores max page size requests larger than 5,000... Dataverse doesn't support the $skip query option'.

Configuration.IncrementalSyncDescription: Two mechanisms. (1) Change tracking (preferred): Prefer: odata.track-changes on first GET; follow @odata.nextLink pages; @odata.deltaLink on last page is the cursor; subsequent polls follow deltaLink verbatim. Requires ChangeTrackingEnabled=true per table. (2) Fallback: modifiedon gt {watermark} ORDER BY modifiedon asc for tables without change tracking.
Configuration.ChangeTrackingNote: Prefer: odata.track-changes on first GET. Follow @odata.nextLink pages (header propagates). Save @odata.deltaLink from last page. Next poll: GET deltaLink verbatim. Deleted records appear with @odata.context /$deletedEntity. Source: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-apps/developer/data-platform/use-change-tracking-synchronize-data-external-systems example showing @odata.deltaLink: '[Org URI]/api/data/v9.0/accounts?$deltatoken=919042...'
Configuration.WebhooksNote: Outbound webhooks from Dataverse to external URL on server events (POST JSON payload). Secured by shared key in header or query string — no HMAC signature. Source: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-apps/developer/data-platform/use-webhooks.
Configuration.BulkOperationsNote: OData $batch: up to 1,000 subrequests. Change sets for transactional atomicity. Content-Type: multipart/mixed. Source: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-apps/developer/data-platform/webapi/execute-batch-operations-using-web-api.

ServiceProtectionLimits.source: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-apps/developer/data-platform/api-limits: 'Number of requests: 6,000 within the five-minute sliding window. Execution time: 20 minutes (1,200 seconds). Number of concurrent requests: 52 or higher.' Note: 'These limits can change and might vary between different environments.'

ErrorResponseShape.description: Top-level 'error' key with 'code' (may be empty) and 'message'. Optional CDS annotations via Prefer: odata.include-annotations='*'.

Configuration.ConcurrencyControlNote: Dataverse auto-generates @odata.etag on all entity GET responses. Supports If-Match/If-None-Match for conditional PATCH (optimistic concurrency). 412 on ETag mismatch. Source: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-apps/developer/data-platform/webapi/perform-conditional-operations-using-web-api: 'Dataverse generates a weakly validating @odata.etag property for every entity instance...ETags to support conditional retrievals, optimistic concurrency.'
Configuration.DeleteSemanticsNote: Most Dataverse tables use statecode deactivation: statecode=0 Active, statecode=1 Inactive. Default for all custom tables. Hard DELETE via HTTP DELETE also exists but permanent. Source: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-apps/developer/data-platform/entity-metadata: 'StateCode: 0 Active / StatusCode 1 Active; 1 Inactive / StatusCode 2 Inactive — the default for custom tables.'

WriteCapability.Note: Full CRUD. POST /api/data/v9.2/{entityset} (create, 204 + OData-EntityId header). PATCH /api/data/v9.2/{entityset}({id}) (update). DELETE /api/data/v9.2/{entityset}({id}) (permanent hard delete). Source: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/power-apps/developer/data-platform/webapi/create-entity-web-api.

Configuration.DefaultConflictResolutionNote: ETag-based optimistic concurrency available, justifying MostRecent IF bidirectional sync is explicitly enabled per-EntityMap.
Configuration.CustomObjectMarkerPattern: IsCustomEntity eq true in EntityDefinitions response; SchemaName has publisher customization prefix (e.g. new_, cr7f_)
Configuration.CustomFieldMarkerPattern: IsCustomAttribute eq true in AttributeMetadata; SchemaName has publisher customization prefix
Configuration.DiscoverFieldsMechanism: GET /api/data/v9.2/EntityDefinitions(LogicalName='{entityLogicalName}')/Attributes — all columns with AttributeType, LogicalName, IsCustomAttribute, IsPrimaryId, MaxLength, Precision.
